record.original_question: For two-dimensional Euler solutions, can one explain why the epsilon-entropy of an ensemble of velocity fields appears to decrease at large times, even though the full fluid phase space also includes particle positions and is not simply the velocity space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a bounded domain (or the torus) $\mathbb{T}^2$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with smooth initial data, and consider an ensemble (probability measure) of such solutions on the space of divergence-free velocity fields. For $\varepsilon>0$, the $\varepsilon$-entropy of a probability measure $\mu$ on a metric space $X$ is defined as $H_\varepsilon(\mu)=\inf\sum_i \mu(A_i)\log(1/\mu(A_i))$, where the infimum runs over measurable partitions $\{A_i\}$ of $X$ by sets of diameter $\le \varepsilon$ (equivalently, the entropy of the discretization of $\mu$ at scale $\varepsilon$ in $X$).

Numerical and heuristic considerations indicate that, when $X$ is taken to be the velocity-field phase space (e.g.\ $L^2_\sigma$ of divergence-free fields), the $\varepsilon$-entropy of the pushforward of an initial ensemble along the Euler flow appears to decrease as $t\to\infty$. However, the genuine phase space of an ideal fluid also includes the Lagrangian particle configuration (the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group), where the flow is measure-preserving and entropy cannot decrease.

Problem. Provide a rigorous explanation, consistent with the volume-preserving (Hamiltonian) nature of the Euler flow on the diffeomorphism group, of why the $\varepsilon$-entropy of an ensemble of two-dimensional Euler velocity fields exhibits decay at large times when measured only on the velocity component of phase space. In particular, identify the mechanism by which information about the velocity is transferred to the particle (Lagrangian) degrees of freedom and quantify this transfer so as to recover an overall non-decreasing entropy on the full phase space.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of explaining apparent entropy decrease for ensembles of 2D Euler velocity fields (Shnirelman-type problem) remains an active research topic. Recent works (e.g., a 2022 Phys. Rev. Fluids paper introducing "hydrodynamic entropy" and a 2024–2026 work on entropy maximization in 2D Euler) study related entropy decrease and mixing phenomena, but no complete rigorous explanation that reconciles velocity-space entropy decrease with the volume-preserving Lagrangian flow has been established.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic entropy and emergence of order in two-dimensional Euler turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: proposes hydrodynamic entropy to quantify order in 2D Euler turbulence and shows that this entropy decreases with time, even though the system is isolated with no dissipation
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature confirms the phenomenon of entropy decrease in 2D Euler ensembles is studied but the mechanism remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Entropy maximization in the two-dimensional Euler equations
status_evidence.snippet: provides the basis of Shnirelman's maximal mixing theory ... variational problem related to entropy maximization in the 2D Euler equations
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2026) work develops Shnirelman's maximal mixing/entropy framework but does not resolve the velocity-vs-full-phase-space entropy paradox.

status_evidence.title: On the Long Time Behavior of Fluid Flows
status_evidence.snippet: introduces key conjectures due to Shnirelman, Šverák and Yudovich regarding long-time behavior
status_evidence.claim: The long-time behavior questions related to this problem are listed as open conjectures.
